title: Make the rate client's retry proxy retry

blocks.text: The billing service gets exchange rates from a remote service through `Retrying.Rates`. The connection drops a few times an hour, so the client is wrapped in a proxy from `Retrying.wrap` that is meant to try a failed call again. The billing code catches `IOException` around every rate lookup and falls back to yesterday's rate; anything else fails the invoice run.
`Retrying.wrap(...)` already builds the proxy. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Retrying.java`: `call(...)`, which makes one call on the proxy happen.

When you're done, a network failure (`IOException` or a subclass) is tried again, up to the number of attempts the proxy was built with. If the last attempt fails too, the billing code gets the rate service's own last exception, so its `catch (IOException e)` still runs. Any other failure reaches the billing code as itself, after one call. About six lines in total.

cases.says: a rate the service gives on the first call is returned after one call
network failures are tried again, and the rate that finally comes back is returned
after the last attempt fails, the caller gets the service's own last IOException, of its own type and message
a failure that is not a network error reaches the caller as itself after one call

origin.section: A Checked Exception the Interface Method Doesn't Declare Reaches the Caller as UndeclaredThrowableException

concepts: Proxy.newProxyInstance generates a class implementing the listed interfaces whose every method call goes to one InvocationHandler, which can serve any interface, the JDK's included.

A checked exception thrown by a handler that the interface method doesn't declare reaches the caller as UndeclaredThrowableException, skipping the caller's catch; unchecked and declared exceptions pass through unchanged.

Method.invoke wraps whatever the target throws in InvocationTargetException, so a handler that tests or rethrows the wrapper retries nothing and changes the type of every failure; it must work with getCause().
